newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE STOCKS WEAKEN ON PROFIT-TAKING.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE STOCKS WEAKEN ON PROFIT-TAKING.

text.p: Continuing profit-taking and fears of possible drought dragged Zimbabwean stocks one percent down on Monday in active trade and brokers said they expected that trend to carry on throughout the week.
The main industrial index dropped 136.71 points -- or 1.2 percent -- to close the day at 11,775.92.

"The market should be firming on a lower inflation figure (for July) and the resumption of World Bank aid," one broker said of annual inflation which was pegged at 19.1 percent in July from 21.4 percent in June.

"But instead sentiment on the market is depressed. Some people feel the market is now overvalued after its recent rise to all time highs while others are overreacting to reports about a possible drought," he added.
"There's selling pressure across the board on the market and I think we are going to continue getting a correction on the index this week," another one said.

On the Zimbabwe Stock Exchange on Monday, cement producer Porthold dropped 150 cents to 2,800, sugar company Hippo shed 90 cents to 1,700, packaging firm Hunyani lost 40 cents to 220, tobacco group TSL traded 25 cents down at 600 and clothing retailer Truworths was 20 cents lower at 730.
Against the trend, coffee and tea producer EHPL and tyre company NTS each rose 25 cents to 250 and 420 respectively.

Minings were also softer despiter a slightly firmer bullion price following Friday's sharp fall in the U.S. stock market. Brokers said investors were monitoring the situation on Wall Street before they rush in to buy gold.
On the Zimbabwean mining board, nickel producer Bindura dropped 75 cents to 450 and Wankie Colliery shed 80 cents to 820.
The mining index lost 70 points to end at 824.17.
